points.description: The answer conveys that DHCP is a network management protocol in which a server dynamically assigns an IP address and other network configuration parameters to devices on the network.

The answer conveys that DHCP is used to simplify end-system configuration by assigning IP addresses automatically (or manually) and supplying extra settings such as DNS server, netmask or default router. Mentioning that it has largely replaced RARP/BOOTP is not required.

rubric.notes: Full marks for explaining both what DHCP is (a protocol where a server dynamically assigns IP addresses and network settings to devices) and what it is used for (simplifying configuration, automatic or manual address assignment, and supplying settings like DNS, netmask or default router). Partial marks are not used because the question is worth only one mark, so each point is all-or-nothing. No marks for a vague description that does not mention automatic assignment of addresses or configuration.
